analyst_view.overall: Early view: Gattuso's Lazio are top and unbeaten after 11 games, but the 1-1 at Napoli cost them Nuno Tavares (a muscle injury that one report calls more serious than first thought) and Sutalo, who also went off with a muscle problem. Zaccagni and Gudmundsson were missing too. Lecce took a point at Torino with a physical, compact display, and with no European games for either side both should be fresh.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, mostly Lazio's. I lean slightly higher: Lazio have scored 25 in 11 and have a 13-point run from five games, while Lecce have conceded 22, a total only four teams have topped. Losing Tavares takes width away from Lazio's attack, so I would not go much past three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. I lean a little lower because Lazio's home games have averaged about 8.2 corners: Gattuso's side attack through quick wide players such as Noslin and Isaksen rather than by piling crosses in. Lecce away games have also averaged under nine.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: Lazio's games do carry plenty of cards, but Lecce's matches have averaged about 2.7, among the lowest in the league, and the report from Torino mentions only one Lecce booking. There is no referee yet; a strict appointment would change this.

shots.text: The site expects 25.7 shots, and that matches both sides' record: Lazio's home games have averaged about 26 and Lecce's away games about 27. Lazio press high and should shoot more, but Lecce's deep block cuts the quality and number of clear looks, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because Lecce allow about 5.6 on target a game, above the league norm, and their away games have averaged over ten. Frattesi's late runs into the box give Lazio a source of clean, close-range efforts.
